context: Make the synchronize evaluation union the base-ref predicate with the PR's own, so a widening protects the PR that introduces it. Have green_unmerged_sweep.py treat an explicitly-disabled auto-merge as a signal to leave alone rather than re-arm - a marker label or a check of who last disabled it. Document that draft is the durable hold. Both files are self-protected, so this lands under owner review.
description: Observed twice in one session. Disabling auto-merge on a PR does not hold: (1) .github/workflows/auto-merge-on-open.yml triggers on 'synchronize', so ANY later push to the branch re-enables it - that is how PR #1528, a privacy change, merged with no review after auto-merge had been explicitly disabled; and (2) nightly.yml runs green_unmerged_sweep.py --apply on a schedule, which re-enables auto-merge on green non-soundness PRs, so a disabled PR silently re-arms overnight even with no pushes. The synchronize re-evaluation uses the BASE-REF copy of the predicate, so a soundness widening still in flight cannot protect the PR that introduces it - which is the specific hole #1529 walked through. The only durable hold today is draft status, which both paths honour (auto-merge-on-open.yml gates on draft == false; green_unmerged_sweep.py requires 'not draft'). That is not discoverable from either workflow's documentation.

preserves.behavior: Drafts continue to be skipped by both paths

work_units.summary: Union the base-ref and PR-copy predicates on synchronize
Stop the nightly sweep re-arming an explicitly disabled auto-merge
Document draft status as the durable hold
